cards.claim: Optimal batch size increases with training time (token budget), not fixed at epoch count
cards.conditions: C4 dataset, 354M parameter MPT model, optimally-tuned learning rate, 1B-275B tokens, warmup-stable schedule
cards.effect: Optimal batch size increases by ~20B tokens when pretraining token budget increases from ~60B to ~275B tokens (approximately proportional to T^0.5)
cards.evidence: Experimental measurement across training curves with loss evaluation at multiple time steps
cards.quote: We observe an increase of the optimal batch size with increase of the pretraining token budget from to (Fig. 3(a))

cards.claim: Fixed batch size becomes suboptimal over training; optimal scaling requires joint data and batch size adjustment, not just learning rate adjustment
cards.conditions: C4 dataset, 354M model, multiple token budgets 1B-275B, various batch sizes
cards.effect: Smaller batch sizes at fixed count are progressively phased out and become suboptimal as training progresses to longer token budgets
cards.evidence: Loss curves across batch sizes split by token budget (Fig. 3b) showing intersection patterns where larger batch sizes eventually dominate
cards.quote: naïve 'pairwise' scaling rules for optimal learning rate, e.g. lr ∝ b^{-1}, are convenient for predicting optimal values at scale, they do not necessarily result in the best model performance: taking batch size dynamics into account is required.

cards.claim: Critical batch size evolves with training time approximately as b_c ∝ T^0.5, affecting optimal hyperparameter scaling regimes
cards.conditions: C4 dataset, MPT models 32M-354M parameters, 1B-275B tokens, µP and standard parametrization
cards.effect: Critical batch size growth of approximately 0.5 power law; this dynamic drives transitions between different optimal learning rate scaling behaviors (lr ∝ b^{-1} vs lr ∝ b^1)
cards.evidence: Fitted power law to critical batch size extracted from bell-curve fits of optimal lr vs batch size at each token budget
cards.quote: we experimentally find (see definition in Sec. 2.1) to evolve in time with α_b ≈ 0.5 and α_crit ≈ 1 (Fig. 2, left)

cards.claim: Optimal learning rate scaling with batch size follows different regimes: inverse scaling (lr ∝ b^{-1}) at low batch sizes shifts to surge scaling (lr ∝ b) at high batch sizes, with transition determined by critical batch size
cards.conditions: C4 dataset, MPT 32M-354M parameters, 1B-275B tokens, AdamW optimizer
cards.effect: Low batch size region: lr_opt decreases as b increases; high batch size region: lr_opt increases as b increases; optimal learning rate drifts by ~2x over 200B token increase depending on batch size regime
cards.evidence: Experimental learning rate optimization across 5D hyperparameter grid, fitted with theoretical model from Li et al. (2024) Eq. 1, shown in Fig. 1(a) and (b)
cards.quote: we observe an intricate drift of the optimal learning rate in time as governed by the batch size value. In a simplified way, for small values we observe a decrease of lr_opt with an increase of the token budget, while for the larger values it is oppositely an increase

cards.claim: Optimal batch size correlates with critical batch size evolution: b_opt ≈ 0.4 * b_c across the measured range
cards.conditions: C4 dataset, 354M model, 1B-275B tokens, optimally-tuned learning rate per configuration
cards.effect: Optimal batch size tracks critical batch size with fixed proportionality, suggesting critical batch size sets the scale for optimal batch size dynamics
cards.evidence: Comparison of optimal batch size from Fig. 3(a) with critical batch size evolution from Fig. 2(left)
cards.quote: we obtain b_opt ≈ 0.4 * b_c for the range of our measurements

cards.claim: Learning rate sensitivity (loss penalty for suboptimal lr) decreases significantly with training time, especially in critical batch size region
cards.conditions: C4 dataset, MPT 32M and 354M models, batch sizes 512-2048 tokens, 1B-275B token budgets, µP and standard parametrization
cards.effect: Up to 5x reduction in learning rate sensitivity per ~40B token budget increase; effect is more pronounced near critical batch size than in extreme regimes
cards.evidence: Loss profile measurements at multiple token budgets showing decreased curvature (measured by normalized loss variation per lr deviation unit)
cards.quote: We observe that there is a general decrease in the learning rate sensitivity by up to 5x per each token budget increase by ~40B tokens

cards.claim: Warmup duration should scale in absolute tokens (fixed token count) with gradient step count adjusted per batch size, not as fixed step count
cards.conditions: C4 dataset, warmup-stable schedule, varying batch sizes and token budgets
cards.effect: Ensures consistent warmup token budget across all batch size configurations; simplifies comparison of learning rate optima across batch sizes
cards.evidence: Experimental design in Sec. 2.4 and validation in Appendix A.7 showing decay phase omission and warmup token fixing does not affect optimal position
cards.quote: Whenever batch size is varied, we adjust the number of gradient steps in the warmup phase accordingly so that the total amount of tokens seen by the model during warmup equals 4B tokens

cards.claim: Critical batch size evolution is not solely determined by loss value; models within µP with same loss can have different critical batch size regions
cards.conditions: C4 dataset, µP model family with same training trajectory (steps, batch size, horizon) but different widths (32M-354M), loss changes comparable between time and width scaling
cards.effect: Critical batch size drifts substantially with token budget (+50% per 80B tokens) but does not drift across µP model widths despite comparable loss changes, indicating additional factors beyond loss
cards.evidence: Observed no significant change of bell-curve shape or peak position (b_c) across µP models at fixed token budget; substantial drift of b_c across token budgets at fixed model; back-of-the-envelope calculation comparing loss changes
cards.quote: this observation brings evidence that dependence of the critical batch size exclusively on the loss value suggested by Kaplan et al. (2020) (Eq. 8) is not entirely complete

cards.claim: Optimal learning rate scaling dynamics (as function of batch size and token budget) are largely preserved within µP across model sizes despite different absolute loss values
cards.conditions: C4 dataset, µP trajectories with base widths 32M and 354M, model sizes 32M-5B parameters, token budgets 1B-275B
cards.effect: Same relative scaling rules for optimal lr apply across the 150x model size range; enables transfer of hyperparameter scaling rules between different model scales
cards.evidence: Averaged results across three µP models for each configuration (Appendix A.11); no significant differences observed despite different model sizes and loss values
cards.quote: Furthermore, we find these dynamics to be largely preserved within µP (Appendix A.11)
